blocks.text:
After twelve years away, Mara steps onto the platform with one suitcase and a letter she has not opened.

The station clock is still seven minutes slow. Some things, she thinks, have learned how to stay.

The man at the ticket window knows her name. He asks if she has come for the shop.

She has come for her father. She does not correct him.
Her father’s shop is exactly as she remembers, except for the map in the window: a careful rendering of Bellwether with a street that does not exist.
Under the familiar loose stone, a brass key waits in an envelope. On the envelope, in her father’s handwriting: “Which way is home?”
The room smells of paper, cedar, and the sea. Every drawer is labeled. One is empty.
Mara walks to the street on the map. The road ends at the water.

notes.text: The impossible street is the first real fracture in the familiar. Keep it small. No explanation yet.
Recurring motifs: maps, inherited silences, the unreliable comfort of familiar places.

resources.title: A note on Bellwether
resources.text: A fictional coastal town. Once a harbor for survey ships; now a place people pass through. The sea is always audible, never quite visible.
